overview.title: Support Ticket Demo
overview.purpose: A synthetic support-ticket workflow accepts a message, classifies its intent, builds a tool plan and returns a small audit event. The example contains no real customer data and makes no claim that its PII controls are sufficient.

docs.title: Support Ticket Demo
docs.purpose: A synthetic support-ticket workflow accepts a message, classifies its intent, builds a tool plan and returns a small audit event. The example contains no real customer data and makes no claim that its PII controls are sufficient.

purpose.text: The name is a control candidate, not proof of authorization enforcement.
A synthetic audit stub; storage and retention are outside this example.
A placeholder classifier, not a production intent model.
Synthetic API boundary for the public handoff example.
An intentionally small planning step; no model is called.
No purpose statement located in approved documentation or module docstrings.

steps.text: `gateway.api.submit` receives the message and email address.
`orchestrator.agent.build_plan` asks an allowed tool for a response.
`audit.events.redact_event` prepares an audit event without the email address.

controls.title: Intent and plan
controls.recommendation: Trace input → structured intent/plan, including ambiguous and failed planning cases.
controls.claim: Names and syntax are leads; runtime, fail-closed behavior and production readiness unverified.

controls.title: Tool authority and scope

limits: Static calls/imports do not prove a runtime request path.
Unique module-suffix bindings assume one indexed local module; dynamic sys.path can load another module.
Function parameters/guards are indexed for Python only; other languages retain file-level blocks.
Control candidates are not a security or production-readiness verdict.
